segments.t: After Samuel's burial at Père-Lachaise, the agency holds a tribute. Gabriel welcomes the guests and introduces Françoise Fabian. Line Renaud then joins in with her own memories. Both actresses loved Samuel, but their rivalry colours the way they remember him. Listen first to their words of affection and loss.
Bonsoir. Au nom d'ASK, je vous remercie d'être venus.
Je laisse la parole à une grande amie de Samuel, Françoise Fabian.
Bonsoir. Il y a quelques semaines, je dînais avec Samuel.
Il a dit quelque chose de merveilleux.
Vous, les acteurs, vous jouez pour ne pas grandir.
Vous jouez pour ne pas mourir.
Samuel, tu nous manques terriblement.
Samou était plein de joie, libre!
Comme on faisait la fête, dans le temps!
Tu nous manques, Samou.
Mais je te promets une chose. Nous continuerons à rire.
Oui, il faut se battre contre le chagrin.
Samuel aimait vraiment rire.
Tu aimais une belle chanson. Celle-là surtout.
Tu disais que c'était notre chanson.
Let's go back through the tribute. Gabriel greets everyone and thanks them for coming.
Bonsoir.
'Good evening.' Remember, this is the greeting for the evening.
Au nom d'ASK, je vous remercie d'être venus.
'On behalf of ASK, thank you for coming.' Literally 'in the name of ASK, I thank you for having come'. A formal phrase for speeches.
Je laisse la parole à une grande amie de Samuel, Françoise Fabian.
'I give the floor to a great friend of Samuel's, Françoise Fabian.' Literally 'I leave the word to'. The word for 'friend' has its feminine ending here, and so does 'great'.
Bonsoir.
'Good evening.' Françoise greets the room in the same way, simply and with dignity.
Il y a quelques semaines, je dînais avec Samuel.

'A few weeks ago, I was having dinner with Samuel.' The same opening can mean there is or ago. Before a number of weeks, it places the dinner in the past; was having dinner sets the scene for what Samuel said.
Il a dit quelque chose de merveilleux.

'He said something wonderful.' Has plus said presents one completed remark. Something is built from some and thing, with a short linking word before wonderful. The description tells us what kind of thing he said.
Vous, les acteurs, vous jouez pour ne pas grandir.

'You actors, you play so you don't grow up.' Françoise quotes Samuel addressing actors as a group. Play links their profession with children's games. The purpose phrase explains what they hope to avoid: growing up.
Vous jouez pour ne pas mourir.
'You play so you don't die.' The same purpose pattern returns. The two words for not sit together before die, because they are denying that action rather than the earlier play.
Samuel, tu nous manques terriblement.
'Samuel, we miss you terribly.' Watch out, this one works back to front. In French you say 'you are missing to us'. The person who is missed is the subject.
Samou était plein de joie, libre!
'Samou was full of joy, free!' Line's pet name makes the memory intimate. Full of links the quality to joy; free adds another description of Samuel, rather than referring to a price.
Comme on faisait la fête, dans le temps!
'How we used to party, back in the day!' The background past again, for something that happened again and again. Literally 'how we used to make the party'.
Tu nous manques, Samou.
'We miss you, Samou.' The same back-to-front verb as in Françoise's speech: the two rivals are saying the same thing.
Mais je te promets une chose.
'But I promise you one thing.' She speaks to Samuel with the casual 'you', as to an old friend.
Nous continuerons à rire.
'We'll keep on laughing.' This is the simple future: the verb 'continue' with a future ending. Line wants laughter, not tears.
Oui, il faut se battre contre le chagrin.
'Yes, we must fight against sorrow.' Françoise takes the floor back, with the expression for 'we must'. The word at the end is a strong one for grief.
Samuel aimait vraiment rire.

'Samuel really loved to laugh.' Loved followed directly by laugh describes something Samuel enjoyed. Really strengthens the memory. Françoise agrees with Line's image of him, while trying to add her own view of their friend.
Tu aimais une belle chanson. Celle-là surtout.
'You loved a beautiful song. This one most of all.' Line has the last word. The word for 'beautiful' is feminine, like the song.
Tu disais que c'était notre chanson.

'You used to say it was our song.' Line uses two action words in the background past. Then the music starts, and the whole room sings Samuel's song together. Let's hear the whole farewell once more. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more.
Bonsoir. Au nom d'ASK, je vous remercie d'être venus.
Je laisse la parole à une grande amie de Samuel, Françoise Fabian.
Bonsoir. Il y a quelques semaines, je dînais avec Samuel.
Il a dit quelque chose de merveilleux.
Vous, les acteurs, vous jouez pour ne pas grandir.
Vous jouez pour ne pas mourir.
Samuel, tu nous manques terriblement.
Samou était plein de joie, libre!
Comme on faisait la fête, dans le temps!
Tu nous manques, Samou.
Mais je te promets une chose. Nous continuerons à rire.
Oui, il faut se battre contre le chagrin.
Samuel aimait vraiment rire.
Tu aimais une belle chanson. Celle-là surtout.
Tu disais que c'était notre chanson.
That's the end of this scene. When you watch it, listen for the back-to-front way of saying 'we miss you'; both Françoise and Line use it. See you next time!
Bonne journée!
